Breaking: Exercise coaching boosts colon cancer survival

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1031 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In 2025, an international trial found that people treated for colon cancer were more likely to be alive eight years later if they had received long-term exercise coaching.
  • The question facing doctors now is less whether people with cancer should exercise, and rather how they should build it into routine care.
  • Yet experts caution that the trial's findings may not apply to every cancer or every patient.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In 2025, an international trial found that people treated for colon cancer were more likely to be alive eight years later if they had received long-term exercise coaching.

The question facing doctors now is less whether people with cancer should exercise, and rather how they should build it into routine care. In the US, that shift is reaching hospital standards. From January 2027, breast cancer centers must screen patients' physical function and recommend exercise or physical therapy where needed.

Yet experts caution that the trial's findings may not apply to every cancer or every patient.

In a recent development, the 2025 trial, called CHALLENGE, was led by the Canadian Cancer Trials Group. It began enrolling patients in 2009 and published its results in 2025.

The trial's 889 participants came from six countries, most from Canada and Australia. All had finished surgery and chemotherapy for stage 2 or 3 colon cancer, which had not spread to distant organs.

According to recent reports, half received only health education materials on exercise and healthy eating. The other half additionally met a physical activity consultant for three years.

In the exercise group, the target was similar to adding 45 to 60 minutes of brisk walking, three to four times a week. The amount and type of activity varied from person to person, said Tormod Skogstad Nilsen, a cancer exercise researcher in Norway. But he said participants achieved lasting increases in their physical activity.

It has been revealed that exercise helped. People in the exercise group were less likely to see their cancer come back, to develop a fresh cancer or to die. In all, 93 had at least one of these setbacks, compared with 131 in the health education group.

Recent findings suggest that in cancer research, living longer usually means a larger share of people is still alive at a given point. It does not promise anyone a set number of extra years.

Eight years after joining CHALLENGE, about 90 of every 100 people in the exercise group were alive, compared with about 83 of every 100 in the health education group. That is about 7% more people alive in the group who had guided exercise.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

For people without cancer, the evidence comes from studies that follow people's habits and health over many years. These can show a link, but not prove cause and effect. Active people may also eat better or smoke less.

It has been revealed that in another 2025 study, more than 85,000 adults in the United Kingdom wore a wrist tracker for a week. Over about six years, those who moved most had a 26% lower risk of 13 cancers, including breast and colorectal cancer, than those who moved least.

Industry observers note that even light activity, such as household chores, was linked to lower risk. The link held after researchers accounted for lifestyle, weight and other health conditions.

Earlier research, based on people's self-reporting, has led to similar conclusions. A 2016 analysis of 1.44 million adults in the US and Europe linked free-time activity to a lower risk of many cancers, largely regardless of weight or smoking.

A trial to prove prevention is unlikely: Many cancers take years to develop, so it would need huge numbers of people followed for a long time.

CHALLENGE included only people with colon cancer. But how it picked participants offers a clue: Before joining, they had to pass a fitness test.

Anna Campbell, a professor of clinical exercise science at Edinburgh Napier University in Scotland, sees that as a guide.

According to recent reports, "I think patients with any other cancer stage II and III who have a reasonable baseline level of fitness and no major comorbidities that would prevent them from undertaking moderate to vigorous activity could be considered for similar interventions," she remarked. Comorbidities are other health conditions.

Nilsen noted some people decline to join exercise trials because they feel too unwell or tired, or do not want to exercise. "Hence, study populations are typically younger, 'healthier', and most times slightly more motivated compared to a clinical population," he remarked.

The coaching aimed to make activity a lasting habit, and Campbell noted that is where the trial's value lies.

"The main success of the study is that it enabled the participants to become independent exercisers staying active in a safe and effective and individualized way," she said.

Nilsen agreed. Helping people become more active "in their own environment," without depending on a well-equipped training center, "would likely lead to more sustainable activity behavioral changes," he mentioned.

He is wary of fixed targets, however. "Exercise should be tailored to each individual and the challenges they face, rather than striving to reach a given minimum of exercise required," though health care resources may not always allow it, he added.

Sources indicate that in a 2024 survey of 549 people with cancer, only one in 10 had been referred to an exercise service. Yet almost three in four thought their oncologist should raise the subject.

It has been revealed that "There are some excellent examples of effective pathways but these are few and far between," mentioned Campbell. Good services bring everyone on board, from surgeons to community fitness instructors.

"Ideally, one person in the clinical setting needs to champion the program to link all the team together.".

It has been revealed that campbell expects CHALLENGE's regular coaching will be cut back in everyday care. Apps and live online group sessions could still work, she stated, if run by properly trained staff.

According to recent reports, one recent study of live online exercise engaged patients from poorer backgrounds, in rural areas and with advanced cancer. "It answered some of the barriers, such as cost, travel and lack of confidence," she said.

Patients can ask their care team what exercise is safe for them and what support exists.

Recent findings suggest that according to Nilsen, a training session can bring structure and organization. "You made it here, despite your feeling unwell or fatigued this morning, so you feel mastery based on that," he mentioned.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Massimo Oddo believes that Italy has plenty of young talent coming through, but has urged for players, clubs and supporters to be more patient and pointed to Francesco Camarda as an example: ‘He needed a steadier path, like Pio Esposito’.

Oddo, who worked with Camarda during his time as Milan Futuro head coach, spoke about the development of young Italian talents in an interview with La Repubblica.

Oddo pointed to teenage sensation Camarda as an example of how not to handle emerging young talents. The Milan striker is still only 18 years of age, but there is a growing feeling that his development has stalled somewhat after his first experiences in senior football.

By the age of 14, Camarda had scored a staggering 485 goals from just 89 matches for Milan’s youth teams with an average of 5.45 goals per game.

He went on to become the youngest player ever to feature in Serie A at the age of 15 and 260 days old. At 16 years and 226 days old, Camarda also became the youngest ever Italian to feature in the Champions League.

He was sent out on loan to Lecce last season with the aim of gaining regular opportunities at Serie A level, and though he did manage to score his first Serie A goal, becoming Lecce’s youngest ever league goalscorer in the process, he was only able to start on seven occasions in the Italian top flight.

It has been revealed that since then, Camarda has returned to Milan, where opportunities are again limited behind club-record signing Goncalo Ramos. The emergence of Alphadjo Cisse has also meant fewer opportunities for Camarda with Milan this season.

Oddo, speaking to La Repubblica, states that Camarda was too impatient to make the step up to Serie A and says that he would have been wise to copy somebody like Pio Esposito, who spent two years on loan in Serie B before bursting onto the scene with Inter and then Italy.

“The talent hasn’t just disappeared, but you have to be patient. I take Camarda as an example, one of the most promising young strikers I have ever seen,” noted Oddo.

“He couldn’t wait and pair for his early jump up to Serie A. He needed a steadier path, like Pio Esposito.”.

But there is already huge speculation about which players will have a long-term future at Old Trafford during his tenure, and which players he will want to bring in to help make his time in the north-west a success.

It has been reported that Pochettino will be given funds to bolster the squad in the January transfer window, with a striker, centre-back and left-back all on the agenda after the club failed to strengthen those positions during the summer.

Reports since his appointment was confirmed last week have linked a number of players from the USMNT to the club, including AS Monaco star Folarin Balogun, who was a key player during their time together for the national team.

But Balogun has barely featured for the Ligue 1 side this season after his Deadline Day move to Everton collapsed after the window had already closed, and that means it would be nigh on impossible for him to be able to come into the club and hit the ground running like they will need him to.

However, there is a very clear option within the USMNT squad that would be a huge upgrade for Man Utd at this stage of the season, and could make an instant impact, and that's left-back Antonee Robinson.

The Fulham star has been linked with a move to the club in the past, and his performances in recent seasons have seen him establish himself as one of the best full-backs in the Premier League, as described by Marco Silva in 2024.

“He’s been great for us. He’s one of the best left-backs in this league.

“It’s not just the way he is able to stop players, but the way he is able help ourselves.

“In open play last season he was the full-back in this league with most assists and this season is probably one of the full-backs with the most assists.

Sources indicate that “He’s a top player and a great professional. He’s a proper athlete and is improving in some defensive positions we want him to improve.

“He’s improving season by season, and week by week you can see he is improving, and we are really proud to have him with us.”.

According to recent reports, robinson battled with some injury issues last season for the Cottagers, but still managed to make 27 appearances in the Premier League. This season he has started nine of their 10 games, showing his availability and quality under Alvaro Arbeloa.

According to recent reports, pochettino will know the 29-year-old well from their time together with the national team, and he will know that he has all the attributes to be able to perform in the way that he needs him to. He's also Premier League-proven, and has shown that he knows how to be effective in the final third too, having registered 10 assists in the 2024/25 season.

His current deal at Craven Cottage is due to expire in June 2028, and while they won't want to sell a key player in the middle of the season, a decent offer could be enough to tempt them. It's also likely that Robinson himself would be open to making the move to a bigger club, and reuniting with a manager who knows him well.

It's a deal that nobody seems to be talking about as an option at the moment. But it's one that would make a lot of sense for Pochettino and the team, and would also fit in with the way INEOS likes to move for Premier League-proven stars over talent from foreign leagues.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By OLIVER HOLT, CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 12:00 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 13:04 EST, 16 November 2026.

It has been revealed that the glum face of Lamine Yamal, head in hands, stared out from the front page of the Spanish sports paper AS as it sat on newspaper stands in Madrid on Monday morning. ‘Fin a la racha,’ the headline stated. The end of the run.

For Spain football fans, England’s 3-2 dramatic victory over the world champions in the Spanish capital on Sunday evening made this akin to a day of mourning, the first time their team had tasted defeat in 44 matches, an end to a gilded period of invincibility.

Industry observers note that for England, the feeling was very different. Because Sunday night in the cauldron of the Metropolitano felt very much like a beginning. Thomas Tuchel has been the head coach for almost two years but this was the moment of his true arrival.

This was the victory that freed us from looking back to the Groundhog Day pain of that World Cup semi-final defeat by Argentina in Atlanta last summer and allowed us to look forward to a future that seems luminous and full of hope.

This was the victory that allowed us to stop blaming Tuchel for what happened four months ago and start looking forwards again, dreaming about the glories that he might yet deliver. This was the victory that validated Tuchel and why the FA hired him in the first place. This was the victory that allowed us to believe he might be the Messiah after all.

It has been revealed that this felt like the moment when he embraced us, with all our quirks and football idiosyncrasies, and we embraced him. He had promised ‘proof of concept’ on the eve of the game and he delivered it with bells on. Tuchel has harnessed the best of the English game and welded it to his principles and the result is intoxicating.

Thomas Tuchel has harnessed the best of the English game to down world champions Spain.

In a recent development, once you have seen England play the way they did for an hour against Spain, you are lost. You are lost to the belief that the 62 years of hurt might really be coming to an end at Wembley in the final of the European Championship in the summer of 2028. You are lost to the idea that, finally, everything is falling into place.

Sources indicate that for the 63 minutes up until the sending off of Elliot Anderson, I have never seen an England performance as good as the one that unfolded in the Metropolitano. Spain are the best team in the world and England outclassed them and stupefied them. They were better than them with the ball and better than them without the ball. They were magnificent.

Because of the context, because of the wonder of the stage, because of the odds they faced, England’s victory over Mexico in the grandeur and the mayhem of the mighty Azteca Stadium during the World Cup might edge Sunday’s performance but for pure football, what England delivered in Madrid demands comparison with the best they have played for many a year.

Industry observers note that this year’s World Cup came just too soon but now Tuchel and England understand each other perfectly. And now England are purring. They have a manager who commands the players’ respect and they have a group of players that commands the respect of the manager.

Yes, it was just a Nations League group game but it was against one of the best national sides the world has ever seen. England worked so ferociously and attacked so fluently and defended so devotedly that they reached a level that drew admiration even from their opponents.

Many, many things will live long in the memory. James Trafford’s miraculous double save in the dying minutes gets better every time I watch it. Ben White’s goal channels the beauty of Carlos Alberto’s strike for Brazil against Italy in the 1970 World Cup Final, too. Let’s hope that strike, and his superb defensive performance, bring an end to the boos that have been his companion of late.

Jude Bellingham was relentless, tireless and glided through the game against Spain.

Tuchel had promised ‘proof of concept’ on the eve of the game and he delivered it.

Industry observers note that and then there was Jude Bellingham. Just when you think you can’t admire him any more than you do, he delivers a performance like the one he produced against Spain, a performance that lifted him above even the exalted firm of the other players on two fine teams.

In a recent development, bellingham was tireless. He was relentless. He glided past challenges. He thundered into tackles. He dominated midfield. He has the heart and the sheer brilliant indomitability that Bryan Robson possessed.

Bellingham has it in him to be England’s greatest ever player. He needs trophies to fulfil that destiny but maybe, finally, trophies are in reach again.

He has the team around him to do it, which Robson never quite had. Jordan Pickford is a good goalkeeper but Trafford might just be better. Ezri Konsa had his best game for England in Spain. White and Lewis Hall were superb at full back. Little more needs to be said about England’s front six. They are as good as any unit in world football.

Recent findings suggest that harry Kane, of course, was the best player in the world last year. Some seem to assume that the Ballon d’Or will inevitably pass to Yamal or Kylian Mbappe next. I think it is more likely to be Bellingham.

The man is a colossus. He is a footballer who has everything. He does not know how to be beaten.

Bellingham saw off Barcelona rival Lamine Yamal - and could beat him to the Ballon d'Or.

With them together, the sky is the limit. And Bellingham has also proved to be a player of immense mental strength. It was not so long ago that people worried about his discipline but the fortitude he showed when he was being targeted by Argentina at the World Cup was the best answer to that.

He and Kane are England’s axis of ambition on the pitch. Tuchel is lucky to have them and they are lucky to have him, too. The coach has reached the point where his tactics and his team-building are bearing fruit.

Industry observers note that now England have a team-manager package that genuinely need fear nobody. The victory against Spain was a rehearsal for the bigger stage of major tournaments. Going down to 10 men after 63 minutes against the best team in the world might not have been in the script but that is what rehearsals are for.

After Sunday night in the Metropolitano, England are ready for their close-up.

What to know about the IIHF Women's Ice Hockey World Championship

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (591 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that since its inception in 1990, the Women's Ice Hockey World Championship has almost always been held in the spring — apart from 2021 and 2022, when the COVID-19 pandemic saw it moved to the summer.
  • The idea is make it easier for all of the world's best players to participate.
  • Industry observers note that "This gives the women's game a unique selling point," International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) President Franz Reindl recently told the SID news agency.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that since its inception in 1990, the Women's Ice Hockey World Championship has almost always been held in the spring — apart from 2021 and 2022, when the COVID-19 pandemic saw it moved to the summer. This year, though, the tournament, being hosted by Denmark from November 6 to November 16, is being held in November for the first time.

The idea is make it easier for all of the world's best players to participate. Since its inception in 2023, the North America-based Professional Women's Hockey League (PWHL), widely considered the world's best, has had to pause its season to allow players to take part in the Worlds. This is no longer necessary, as the PWHL's regular season doesn't open until December.

Industry observers note that "This gives the women's game a unique selling point," International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) President Franz Reindl recently told the SID news agency. "Because the PWHL season begins after this, we can be certain that the very best players are participating.".

Previously, the teams were divided into a stronger group and a weaker group, with the idea being to avoid, as much as possible, lopsided scores. This is because women's hockey is not as balanced as the men's game, with Canada or the United States having won every tournament since its inception.

Under the old system, all five teams in the stronger Group A advanced to the quarterfinals. Under the fresh format, four of the five teams advance from both groups. This also sees powerhouses the US and Canada in separate groups, meaning the marquee matchup can't occur early in the tournament.

Group A: USA, Czechia, Switzerland, Germany, Austria.

Group B: Canada, Finland, Sweden, Japan, Denmark.

Industry observers note that no. While the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) ruled on October 30 — a week before the opening faceoff of the Women's Ice Hockey World Championship — that the IIHF must allow Russia back into its tournaments during the 2026-2027 season, it made no mention of this tournament. Under the CAS ruling though, the IIHF will be required to include Russia at the 2027 tournament in Quebec City.

It has been revealed that as noted above, either Canada or the United States has won every edition of this tournament — and indeed the two countries have split Olympic gold medals between them (Canada with five, USA with three) since the sport was introduced to the Winter Games in 1998. There is nothing to suggest that this is about to change in Herning and Esbjerg, although Canada enters the tournament with a vastly different roster from the one that won Olympic silver in Milano in February.

Among those looking to break this North American domination are Finland, the only other team ever to have made it to a world championship final and Switzerland, who took bronze in Milan.

The United States and Canada will play in generic kits provided by the International Ice Hockey Federation's official supplier due to an ongoing commercial rights dispute.

The Canadian federation, Hockey Canada, said in a statement on Wednesday that its players would be wearing jerseys designed by True Hockey instead of their Bauer jerseys featuring the national team logo. USA Hockey has confirmed that its players too will be wearing jerseys without its national emblem.

"While we have yet to see the jersey Canada will be playing in on Friday, our team remains focused on the tournament and representing our country proudly on and off the ice," Hockey Canada remarked.

Former Manchester United captain Ashley Young has revealed what Mauricio Pochettino needs to be a success at Old Trafford, while speaking exclusively to GIVEMESPORT.

The Red Devils unveiled the arrival of the 54-year-old on a two-and-a-half-year contract last week, replacing Michael Carrick in the dugout after a poor start to the season which has left the club sitting 18th in the Premier League with just one win in their opening ten games.

Pochettino has left his role as the USMNT boss to take over, declaring it a dream come true for him to finally step into the dugout at Old Trafford, with his first game in charge to come on Sunday afternoon against arch-rivals Liverpool at Anfield.

Pochettino was a somewhat surprising appointment, having signed a latest long-term contract with US Soccer following the World Cup last summer. But he is someone that Man Utd have been linked with on a number of occasions over the years, although they have opted to go in alternative directions previously.

The Argentine is best known for his time in charge at Tottenham, where he helped guide them to a runners-up finish in the Premier League and Champions League, while he has also been manager at Espanyol, Southampton, Paris Saint-Germain and Chelsea.

Coming into Man Utd is a substantial task, especially with their current situation, but there are ways Pochettino can revolutionise Man Utd, and when asked for his thoughts on the appointment, Young told GIVEMESPORT that he feels it could be a good hire if he is given control over certain things.

"For me I think that it was an appointment that they've obviously looked at different managers out there who were out of work, but they've looked at what he did, especially when he was at Tottenham," he mentioned.

Industry observers note that "But for me it was one of them where he's had a rebuild at Tottenham, but it took two or three years. But then he's got Tottenham from lower in the league to third in the league, second in the league, Champions League final. So it does show that he's got that pedigree.

Recent findings suggest that "He's even remarked that he always wanted to come back to the Premier League. He loved the Premier League.

"I think it's an appointment where things can go well, but if he's got the control of players coming in, players going out, and the board really give him the confidence and back him.".

Young spent eight-and-a-half years at Man Utd as a player, having joined from Aston Villa as a winger before eventually becoming a regular at full-back.

During his time at Old Trafford, he made 261 appearances, scoring 19 goals, and won the Premier League, FA Cup, League Cup, Community Shield and Community Shield before joining Inter Milan and winning Serie A under Antonio Conte.

He then returned to England for spells with Aston Villa and Everton before dropping into the Championship to help Ipswich Town earn promotion to the Premier League, before retiring this summer.

Former Liverpool, Aston Villa, and England star David James has told GIVEMESPORT who his most underrated teammate was during his career.

The iconic goalkeeper made 572 appearances in the Premier League during his career, representing the Reds, Villa, Portsmouth, West Ham, and Man City, and kept 172 clean sheets, putting him second on the all-time list behind just Chelsea icon Petr Cech.

James also featured 53 times for the England senior team, and was the number one goalkeeper at Euro 2004 and World Cup 2010, while he was also part of the squad in the 2006 World Cup.

During his career, James featured in four FA Cup finals, winning once with Portsmouth, while he also won the EFL Cup with Liverpool, and was teammates with a host of top stars including the likes of Ballon d'Or winner Michael Owen, Robbie Fowler, Ian Rush, John Barnes, David Beckham, Steven Gerrard, Frank Lampard, Rio Ferdinand, Wayne Rooney, and more.

Sources indicate that all of those superstars are considered to be legends of the game in their own right, and could widely be considered to be the best players he ever played alongside. But in every team, there are also players who are equally as important but don't get the same attention.

Recent findings suggest that having played at a number of different levels and leagues, James was able to experience football in all it's forms. He even spent a season playing in India as a player-manager, which saw him experience football in a completely different way.

But while speaking to GIVEMESPORT, on behalf of LiveFootballTickets, James was asked to name who his most underrated teammate was in his playing career, and he knew exactly which former colleague deserved to receive their flowers.

“There’s many, because you know what football’s like: there has to be a star, and other people get a little bit lost in that moment.

Sources indicate that "If I chose England, it would probably be Gareth Barry. That midfield was awash with what we could call superstars in many respects, and Gareth was up there, possibly not playing for the most fancied teams at the time, particularly when he was at Villa.

According to recent reports, "Until James Milner turned up, Gareth was pretty much ever-present in the Premier League. He was a top-drawer player for England, and I don’t think he necessarily got the credit he deserved.

Sources indicate that "Steve McManaman is another one I mentioned before, although he went on to win Champions Leagues in Spain and was well regarded over there. But I’d probably say Gareth Barry.

"He was happy to do the dirty work and he was a lovely guy as well, which is always nice.".

James and Barry played alongside each other for both Aston Villa and England a combined 87 times throughout their careers, winning 39 times.

The central midfielder went on to become the player with the most appearances in Premier League history during his career, surpassing the legendary Ryan Giggs, before James Milner overtook him in his final campaign while at Brighton in 2025/26.

Barry also earned 53 caps for England, scoring 3 goals, while he won the FA Cup and Premier League titles during his time at Manchester City. He retired in 2020 after a spell with West Brom.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Gotham FC will play Sunday's NWSL semifinal against the Kansas City Current at Icahn Stadium over concerns about the quality of the pitch at Sports Illustrated Stadium, which was described as "atrocious" during the team's quarterfinal win over the Seattle Reign.

The NWSL Shield winners declared the venue shift on Monday, less than a week before the semifinal. Icahn Stadium is a smaller venue on Manhattan's Randall's Island that seats 5,000 and has been sparingly used by Gotham, who have played the vast majority of their home games at Sports Illustrated Stadium in Harrison, N.J. since 2021. Sports Illustrated Stadium seats 25,000 and welcomed nearly 13,000 for Sunday's 1-0 win over the Reign.

Sources indicate that the quarterfinal match, though, was marred by complaints about the playing surface from both teams. Reign head coach Laura Harvey described the field as "shit" in a post-match interview with ESPN, while captain Jess Fishlock called it "atrocious." Gotham head coach Juan Carlos Amoros also apologized for the quality of the surface after the NWSL fined the club $10,000 in the build-up to the quarterfinal match.

Sources indicate that "We as a team worked extremely hard to earn a home playoff berth," captain Tierna Davidson stated in a statement on Monday. "What we got was a field that is not the standard this club, this league, or our fans deserve. The quality of the game is not up for debate, so we've made the difficult decision to move to Icahn Stadium on Sunday. A smaller stadium means many of you will not be there, and that is the hardest part of this decision. You have turned every ground where we have played into home, and that does not change on Sunday. We have never needed a perfect setting to make a place ours. Bring everything you have on Sunday, and we will leave it all on the field.".

The pitch at Sports Illustrated Stadium appeared to show the wear and tear from recent events, not least of which was Gotham's regular season slate. Gotham are the secondary tenants at the venue, which is owned by New Jersey's Hudson County but counts MLS' Red Bull New York as the primary tenants and operators of the facility. The stadium was also the site of a rugby doubleheader the weekend before Gotham's quarterfinal against the Reign, which led Gotham midfielder Jaelin Howell to describe the surface as "sandy" and "unstable.".

Recent findings suggest that the Red Bulls will still play a friendly on Saturday at Sports Illustrated Stadium against Club America. The friendly will take place during the men's international break, so several first-team players will miss the match, which will serve as the final game of their season since they missed out on the MLS Cup playoffs for a second season in a row.

"We wish Gotham FC the best of luck in their semifinal at Icahn Stadium," Red Bull Newly introduced York told CBS Sports in a statement. "We look forward to our match on Saturday at Sports Illustrated Stadium.".

Sources indicate that gotham have staged two games at Icahn Stadium in the last year and change – a Concacaf W Champions Cup group stage match in 2025 and their 3-2 win over the Reign in July. There is the perception of convenience for the club's fans based in the city of Fresh York, who would otherwise have to trek to New Jersey to attend a game. As far as public transportation goes, though, Icahn Stadium is only accessible via the M35 bus; a footbridge connecting Randall's Island to 125th Street is also an option, as is driving to the stadium.

Sources indicate that "It's nice for folks who live in New York to have a somewhat closer venue," Jen Muller, a longtime member of the official Gotham supporters group Cloud 9, told CBS Sports last year. "I know it's not ideal for a lot of them, too, because there's one bus that comes here, but you adapt.".

The pitch at Icahn Stadium, which has also hosted New York City FC II matches this year, is not expected to be an issue and was not during the Concacaf match in 2025.

"I don't really want to talk too much about it, but the Sports Illustrated Stadium has traditionally been the best pitch in the league," Amoros noted at the time, "and the last couple of games, it's definitely been far away from that, so this pitch here is outstanding.".

Gotham's move to Icahn comes despite the fact that they avoided a scheduling conflict with Sunday's results. The NWSL's broadcast slots for this year's semifinals were Saturday at 12 p.m. ET on CBS and Paramount+ and Sunday at 3 p.m. ET on ABC; the Washington Spirit will host the Utah Royals on Saturday, while Gotham will take on the Current on Sunday.

For Gotham, the Sunday time slot was the preferred option because of a pre-existing scheduling conflict with the Red Bulls' Saturday friendly against Club America. They had to wait out the result of the Spirit's quarterfinal with the Portland Thorns, though, since the Thorns would have been unable to host a semifinal at 9 a.m. local time. Gotham seemed destined to return to Sports Illustrated Stadium once they avoided the scheduling conflict but the quality of the pitch caused fresh concerns.

The Spirit, meanwhile, avoided a scheduling conflict of their own. They were originally set to host the Royals at Northwest Stadium in Landover, Md., home of the NFL's Washington Commanders, because their usual venue of Audi Field was instead hosting Secretaries' Cup, a Division III college football game between the United States Merchant Marine Academy and the United States Coast Guard Academy. The college football game has since been pushed to a later slot that day, Spirit CEO Kim Stone crediting Audi Field owners D.C. United and sponsor Lafayette Federal Credit Union for underwriting "the additional costs necessary to bring this semifinal match home.".

In a recent development, the challenges stem from the fact that many NWSL teams are secondary tenants in their home stadiums, the Spirit included – MLS' D.C. United own and operate Audi Field. Some, like the Royals and the Orlando Pride, benefit from sharing ownership groups with MLS clubs, while the Current own and operate CPKC Stadium. The rest often rent the local MLS team's stadium, Gotham and the Spirit included, but it creates other unique conflicts for teams with more control over their venues. The Current's quarterfinal against Angel City on Saturday, for example, kicked off at 11 a.m. local time in order to fit the broadcast slot on CBS.

A grant to hand out more grants — and build a research area

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Grants worth up to US$10,000 will fund niche scientific problems.Credit: SimpleImages/Getty.
  • Amid political instability and decreased funding for science worldwide, some non-profit organizations are testing whether and how microgrants — awards of US$10,000 or less — can spur innovation.
  • The initiative will, in early 2027, award at least 50 individuals — called field builders — $70,000 each.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grants worth up to US$10,000 will fund niche scientific problems.Credit: SimpleImages/Getty.

Amid political instability and decreased funding for science worldwide, some non-profit organizations are testing whether and how microgrants — awards of US$10,000 or less — can spur innovation. The latest development comes from the Experiment Foundation, a non-profit science funding organization in Berkeley, California, which has launched the Field Building Accelerator to cultivate ingenuity hubs around specific fields of research using small, rapidly deployed grants.

The initiative will, in early 2027, award at least 50 individuals — called field builders — $70,000 each. The recipients, in turn, will design their own microgrant programme to distribute up to $10,000 to researchers exploring distinct facets of the same niche scientific problem. The grants will be hosted on Experiment.com, an online platform that allows organizations to advertise and fund research projects.

“We want to create a different persona in science — the people who can chart new research territory,” claims David Lang, executive director of the Experiment Foundation.

The accelerator programme is open to proposals that broadly target oceans, climate, toxicity, future science and conservation technology, says Lang — reflecting the interests of its funders, including non-profit organizations such as the Gordon and Betty Moore Foundation in Palo Alto, California. Prospective field builders must propose a name for the field, define its core questions and challenges, and identify at least eight researchers, laboratories or communities they would consider funding.

Recent findings suggest that judges will select field builders who they think are best placed to identify overlooked talent, back unproven ideas and bring like-minded researchers together. Ideally, says Lang, they will reflect diverse scientific perspectives, including early-career researchers, science journalists, science-fiction authors and venture capitalists. “There are people that build momentum in scientific fields, but they are different from the ones who are getting substantial publications or spinning out companies,” he says.

And, in a bid to take chances on unconventional ideas, the judges will not average scores; instead, if any of the two or three judges champions an application, it moves forward.

According to recent reports, although some might baulk at the idea that $10,000 grants are large enough to spur latest research disciplines, others say it is time to experiment with new ways to distribute research funding. “If we really want to help to seed challenging, high risk, ‘who knows what will happen’ ideas, then small-scale grants are a good strategy,” says Brian Nosek, executive director of the Center for Open Science, a non-profit organization in Charlottesville, Virginia, that promotes transparent and reproducible science.

Industry observers note that in 2025, The Science Foundation in Seattle, Washington, organized public donations to award up to $10,000 to researchers who have a compelling ‘what if’ basic-science proposal in the areas of mathematics, physical sciences and biological sciences. The foundation announced the second round of winners on 12 November.

Bundesliga treat Harry Kane's Ballon d'Or as beacon of hope as Germany's competitiveness questions linger

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2108 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Even if the hints of a smile never fully leave his face, there is an overriding sense of practicality when Philipp Lahm speaks.
  • It has been revealed that "It helped Harry Kane and Michael Olise that they came from another country," Lahm noted four days after Kane's massive win.
  • Sources indicate that A quick glance at the data would confirm the hypothesis.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Even if the hints of a smile never fully leave his face, there is an overriding sense of practicality when Philipp Lahm speaks. He seems to have shed the intensity associated with the life of a professional athlete nearly a decade after retiring, but the characteristics of a World Cup-winning captain are hard to miss. He is friendly and open but also serious, so when the topic of conversation shifts to Harry Kane's Ballon d'Or triumph, he is politely unflinching in his assessment of what the award means for soccer in Germany.

It has been revealed that "It helped Harry Kane and Michael Olise that they came from another country," Lahm noted four days after Kane's massive win. "I think it's quite difficult for a German player playing in the Bundesliga [to win the Ballon d'Or].".

Sources indicate that A quick glance at the data would confirm the hypothesis. The last Bundesliga-based player and the last German player to win the sport's most prestigious individual award was Borussia Dortmund's Matthias Sammer in 1996. A German player has only finished inside the top three of the Ballon d'Or three times since, the last being Manuel Neuer in 2014, while Kane is only the seventh Bundesliga player to rank in the top three since Sammer's win. Lahm seamlessly links the pattern to another less-than-ideal trend in Germany's top flight -- Bayern Munich, with whom he won eight Bundesliga titles, are the division's indisputable kings.

They have lost the title just once since the 2012-13 season, a lack of competitiveness at the top of the table a natural consequence of their dominance. This is, in some ways, not Bayern's problem, but a narrative persists in Germany regardless. Players have historically been unable to reach the peaks of the game in Germany because of the circumstances, inspiring a wide-ranging set of side effects. Kane's move to Bayern was not designed to be anything other than the right move at the right time for a player talented enough to compete for the UEFA Champions League, but three years later, those invested in the Bundesliga's success are beginning to treat him as a beacon of hope.

"I do hope that the good players stay in the Bundesliga," Lahm said, "so I'm hopeful through Harry Kane that a lot of other players will follow because it's possible to win and play here.".

In a recent development, the argument to join Bayern Munich is a straightforward one, if you ask sporting director Christoph Freund -- "you can win titles with us," both in Germany and Europe. Bayern have won the Champions League twice in the last 14 years, a feat matched only by Paris Saint-Germain and topped by Real Madrid. The Bundesliga's distribution of wealth favors them in this case, to the point that it likely played a sizable role in signing Kane and Olise. The balance of financial power in the European club game, though, has shifted as Bayern re-established their foothold in Germany -- the Premier League has become the sport's league of choice because it has the financial might to back up the claim. Players like Robert Lewandowski and Mario Gotze used to prove their worth at other German clubs (and in their specific case, Borussia Dortmund) before climbing up the food chain and joining Bayern. Florian Wirtz's jump from Bayer Leverkusen to Liverpool in 2025, though, is an example of a latest world order, one some hope Kane's Ballon d'Or might change.

"It's all about the attention, so when you're successful with the German national team that's visible, but then when you play also successful soccer with Liverpool, then the attention in U.K. is much bigger," Lahm said, citing Wirtz's hypothetical Ballon d'Or case as an example, "so that would be more difficult for a German player in the Bundesliga alone, rather than changing to somewhere else outside and being successful abroad.".

The Bundesliga's international appeal has not only taken a hit on the sporting side in recent years. Bayern's executives believe their club makes up around 50% of the league's brand value globally, and though they are unapologetic about their strengths on the pitch, they also argue they are doing too much of the heavy lifting. Rouven Kasper, a member of Bayern's executive board, pointed to Premier League clubs' oversized presence on preseason tours as a primary example for the Bundesliga to follow but all but questioned the league's interest in the strategy.

"The league needs to be, as well, stronger and bring more reach, but the league exists from the clubs," Kasper remarked. "We are the spearhead of German football, and I think together with the other clubs and together with the league, we need to be even more active in the markets ... it's not enough, and at the end, it's about people, community. We want to be approachable. We want to talk to the people. We want to be there, as the Bundesliga and Bayern alone cannot do it together with Dortmund, so we need more activities from the league and being in different markets, as the U.K. guys are doing and also the Spanish guys are doing. We will do our part.".

Their part includes potentially using Kane as a hook for player recruitment, even if other leagues have their charms for the world's top talents.

"I think everybody knows the Premier League is the biggest league at the moment," Freund said. "Also, Spain is really attractive with Real Madrid and Barcelona, but we know we are Bayern Munich and the German Bundesliga is also really a strong league, a really good league, outstanding stadiums, outstanding atmosphere, and you can [perform] also on a very high level like Harry, the next step in his career, and therefore, I think Bayern Munich and also the German Bundesliga is very attractive, also, for international top players.".

Some in the Bundesliga, though, are resigned to the fact that there are certain things Bayern -- and other European clubs -- will simply beat them to. Dortmund have held strong in their attempts to mount a title challenge this season, level on points with Bayern after eight games thanks to Saturday's 2-2 draw in Der Klassiker. For the foreseeable future, though, recruitment of elite talents cannot and will not play a central role in their quest to win silverware. "We never refuse, or we never avoid to tell you guys where we are from, but in comparison to Munich, Madrid, London, Paris, Milan, we are from Dortmund and from a purely economic perspective, we are far behind them," Borussia Dortmund CEO Carsten Cramer stated. "If they [are] just interested in trophies and silver, if they look for the Ballon d'Or player wearing a black and yellow shirt, maybe that is something we can't offer to them.".

While Bayern's brand is wrapped in the quiet luxury of their domestic stronghold, Cramer argued that Dortmund's appeal is a qualitative one.

Recent findings suggest that "In the last 13 years, we didn't become champion but though we didn't become champion, the interest in Dortmund is still increasing and the amount of people following our club on social media and wherever we travel in the world is quite huge," he remarked. "We are able to offer a different approach: closeness. That is the Dortmund way, and I think that is maybe one of the reasons that many, many hardcore supporters of one club do have a sympathy for us as a second-love club, which I do not complain about, and that is our way. I don't want to make us too small by saying we are a niche club, but we are for sure a bit different, and I don't complain about [it].".

Recent findings suggest that patrick Owomoyela, a defender for Jurgen Klopp's Dortmund team that won back-to-back Bundesliga titles more than a decade ago, can clearly map out the recipe to beat Bayern to the top. Strong squad composition and compatibility go a long way, and he believes the current iteration of Dortmund has that -- he praised head coach Niko Kovac's defensive structure and commended him for "sprinkling the creativity" into the team in the months since taking the job in January 2025. There is just one problem, though.

Recent findings suggest that "Even though you know the recipe, the soup is not always the same," he stated. "Even though you put in the same ingredients, it's not always tasting the same, and if it does, maybe it's not the perfect soup, you know? So you need to find that special something.".

Much like Cramer, Owomoyela has a qualitative argument of his own to make when it comes to breaking Bayern's decades-long dominance in the Bundesliga. The "special something" for his Dortmund team was a sense of camaraderie, the foundation of which was Klopp's joyous approach, though he openly admitted that is a difficult thing to replicate.

"This is sometimes the mentality of the guys or the personality of the guys and how that fits together, on top of the stuff that they can do with the ball and as I noted, we weren't the best in terms of playing football," he said. "We were the best team. We had the most fun. We really liked doing a lot of stuff together. We were like a family, and you don't find that all the time, and it gets harder, I would say, every year because football has changed. The intends of players nowadays are totally different ... These guys have a plan, so they want to be part of something for this period of time, but then they want to move on, and that makes it, of course, hard to find that chemistry because he is gone next year.".

Industry observers note that it is the issue he identified with Leverkusen, the Bundesliga's last champion not named Bayern. Their rise up the ranks in the 2023-24 season was ambitious and impressive, but two years later, the mainstays of their title-winning campaign were elsewhere. Wirtz left for Liverpool, as did Jeremie Frimpong, Granit Xhaka now finds himself at Sunderland, Piero Hincapie now plays for Arsenal and then-head coach Xabi Alonso made a stop at Real Madrid before landing at his current post at Chelsea. Jonathan Tah, meanwhile, went the old-school route and now plays at Bayern. The next challenger to Bayern's throne will likely face the same fate for the foreseeable future, no matter whether its stars move to Munich or settle in England.

Saturday's draw between Bayern and Dortmund, though, has offered a flicker of optimism that the Bundesliga might have a title race on its hands before the next great team gets stripped for parts. The 2-2 scoreline flatters Dortmund -- Bayern racked up 4.48 expected goals and were unlucky when the crossbar denied them on both Kane's second-half penalty and a late strike from Lennart Karl, while the visitors generated just 0.74 xG. Owomoyela argued, though, that Bayern have their flaws.

It has been revealed that "What's it gonna take to take that away from Bayern after all these years again?" he asked. "It's just to believe that it's possible and I think the Bayern team revealed in this season as well, or especially maybe, that you can wound them, you can hurt them and something is possible. You can see that in almost every game they played, even in that cup game [against second-division side Magdeburg on Oct. 28] that they just had and they won it 6-1 ... They hit the post, hit the crossbar, scored a goal, had two other significant chances so now take a team with more quality, with the right kind of belief, there might be something possible.".

Industry observers note that saturday's Klassiker only added to the Bundesliga's week of good news, presenting a different case of the league's strengths than Kane's Ballon d'Or triumph, one that will likely take precedence in the short term. The longer Dortmund keep pace with Bayern, the more intriguing the Bundesliga becomes, and at this stage of the season, the possibility of a genuine title race is easy enough to dream up. That sense of optimism, though, tends to give way to the league's current realities. Even if Dortmund answered the question in the affirmative once, there's a long way to go until anyone can definitively say that Bayern can be topped.

"We weren't really eye-level competitors," Owomoyela said about Dortmund's ability to compete with Bayern in the years since their back-to-back Bundesliga titles. "We were there and we were able to hunt, but from a little distance, and I think everybody understands that.".

Aston Villa midfielder Amadou Onana has signed a new five-year contract, extending his existing deal by two years and committing his future to the club alongside manager Unai Emery.

Onana is an unusual modern footballer. Coaches regularly complain about how few vocal leaders there are among the current generation yet Onana is never afraid to speak up.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Juan Sebastian Veron believes that the sky is the limit for Como and Argentina star Nico Paz, whom he tips to reach the game’s highest possible heights: ‘At 22, he does things I’ve only seen Messi and Diego Maradona do’.

The former Sampdoria, Parma and Lazio midfielder spoke in-depth about the qualities and potential that Nico Paz possesses in an interview with La Gazzetta dello Sport.

Nico Paz has established himself as one of the finest players in Serie A over the last two seasons, has recently introduced himself on the Champions League stage and is now being tipped for greatness by legendary former players in his homeland.

The Como attacker provided 12 goals and seven assists with Como last season, and already has six goals and eight assists from 14 appearances at club level in 2026-27.

Back in Argentina, he is one of the leading candidates to inherit Lionel Messi’s legendary no.10 shirt for the national team, for whom he has scored five goals in five games this season.

“Nico Paz has incredible talent. The future is all his if he continues to act with his current level of professionalism,” stated Veron in his interview with La Gazzetta dello Sport.

Veron would later explain that comparing young players to Messi and Maradona has been the ‘death’ of several young Argentine forwards, but he feels that Nico Paz has earned the right to those comparisons.

“At 22, he does things that I’ve only seen Messi and Diego Maradona do. I don’t mean to say that he will reach those levels, defining an era like Diego and Leo did, but Nico Paz has the qualities to attempt the feat. And I wish him success in achieving that goal.”.

It has been revealed that veron believes that Nico Paz has two standout traits: “The personality he shows on the pitch and the way he is able to make plays so naturally. You can tell he has that personality because his teammates always look for him, give him the ball even when he’s being marked, knowing he’ll dribble past opponents and leave them for dust.

Industry observers note that “Nico is a leader in the way he moves, the way he occupies space on the pitch and the way he handles certain moments of play. He chooses when to speed up or slow down depending on the state of play, he can attack from the right, left, through the middle. He’s always at the core of the game.”.

Veron was asked if he sees any of the qualities that he possessed as a player in Nico Paz.

Industry observers note that “I don’t like to make comparisons with players from different eras, but I think that Nico Paz is like if you moved Veron 20 metres further forward. Looking for shots, goals and assists and that last ball in behind,” he replied.

“He brings a lot of value to Argentina, which is trying to rebuild in the post-Messi era. He’s definitely more of a striker and less of a midfielder when you compare him to me, but he also reads the game well and understands the rhythm of it in his head.”.

Despite his earlier claims, Veron warns that making comparisons to legendary former players can often be detrimental.

Industry observers note that “I know Lionel Scaloni well. He’s right to want to divert media attention away from Nico Paz. We’re incredible at burning talent in Argentina. If only you knew how many no.10s with great potential have been ‘killed’ by comparisons to Maradona. It takes patience and a bit of luck.”.

Veron was also asked for his thoughts on Fiorentina’s Franco Mastantuono.

“I can’t know whether he’ll become a superstar or not, but I do think that Serie A is the most suitable league for a player like him,” he noted.

“He has the chance to gain experience, to feel the studs of opposition defenders, to learn the technical and tactical traits that Italians are masters at teaching.

Preparing for 45C: How Germany tests its crisis response

📅 05 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (747 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Imagine a situation in which prolonged drought has devastated Germany and much of Europe, taking a toll on people's lives, the environment and economy — with a heat wave with temperatures of up to 45 degrees Celsius (113 degrees Fahrenheit) compounding the situation.
  • About 180 organizations across Germany, including more than 60 ministries at the state level and nearly 20 federal authorities, are taking part in a major crisis exercise known as LÜKEX 26, which is built around this very scenario.
  • It is Germany's cross-government crisis management exercise organized by the Federal Office of Civil Protection and Disaster Assistance (BBK).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Imagine a situation in which prolonged drought has devastated Germany and much of Europe, taking a toll on people's lives, the environment and economy — with a heat wave with temperatures of up to 45 degrees Celsius (113 degrees Fahrenheit) compounding the situation.

About 180 organizations across Germany, including more than 60 ministries at the state level and nearly 20 federal authorities, are taking part in a major crisis exercise known as LÜKEX 26, which is built around this very scenario.

It is Germany's cross-government crisis management exercise organized by the Federal Office of Civil Protection and Disaster Assistance (BBK). And it's been up and running for more than two decades.

In a recent development, the first LÜKEX in 2004 dealt with the scenario of an extreme winter with a major power outage. Lessons from that exercise proved valuable in 2005 when the Münsterland region of North Rhine-Westphalia — Germany's most populous state — experienced the worst power outage in the country's postwar history. When heavy snowfall caused power lines to collapse, leaving 250,000 people without electricity for days, there was a better understanding of who to contact and where the bottlenecks were.

In a recent development, since it first started, LÜKEX has trained for scenarios involving terror attacks, an influenza pandemic, biological health threats, storm floods in northern Germany and gas shortages in southern Germany. The most recent exercise in 2023 simulated a cyberattack targeting government operations.

With the help of other ministries, the German Weather Service and the Federal Institute of Hydrology, the BBK developed a drought risk analysis to serve as the scenario.

Participants, which include aid organizations Malteser and the German Red Cross, didn't know the specifics of the challenges they would be facing until the exercise kicked off on Wednesday.

Recent findings suggest that at that point, they were told it was July 20, 2027. In that simulated future, they find themselves in a Germany that has been struggling with extreme heat for weeks; water levels in rivers are falling, food supplies are becoming scarce and emergency services are under growing pressure.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Patrick Pöhler, spokesperson for Malteser, remarked additional details include supermarkets having run out of water, collapsed supply chains and skyrocketing prices to enter a swimming pool. He said the scenario also goes into how the situation is impacting sections of society.

"Emergency services and elderly care are areas that require particular attention," Pöhler said. "The increasingly extreme summers of recent years have shown how severely heat can affect staffing levels and operational capacity.".

In its scenario, the northern port city of Hamburg is tasked with managing the disruption of key transport routes that are impacting access to food and drinking water, as well as handling disinformation attacks that are fueling public fear.

According to recent reports, "We have not conducted an exercise of this magnitude since the end of the Cold War. Yet such preparations are essential to strengthen our resilience and crisis-response capabilities," said Hamburg's minister for the interior, Andy Grote.

LÜKEX is designed to test and strengthen the country's ability to manage major crises at a strategic level. No matter the specific scenario, they all help test internal structures, workflows and decision-making processes.

"The lessons learned are continuously incorporated into improving preparedness, planning and cooperation in civil protection," mentioned BBK spokesperson Katharina Böcker.

It has been revealed that this year's topic was decided a long time ago, well before recent summers in which Germany experienced extreme heat, she added. Thousands of people died from heat-related causes during the hot months of this year.

"Crises such as extreme heat waves and prolonged droughts can affect large parts of the population and challenge the operational capabilities of our critical structures over an extended period," said Christian Reuter, secretary general of the German Red Cross, another organization taking part.

Observers take note of how organizations react in the crisis scenario to find out what went well and where things didn't run smoothly.

"We are explicitly encouraged to make mistakes," said Malteser's Pöhler, because that is how weaknesses can be identified and addressed.

A first internal debrief is scheduled for Friday, he added.

A preliminary report with the main findings and respective recommendations is due to be published in the first quarter of next year. A full evaluation report will then be released later in the third quarter of 2027.

Leaving Highbury was a wrench for Arsenal in 2006, but it was not the case 20 years later. They could not wait to get out of the stadium with the same name after a night that left Mikel Arteta looking haunted.

Fleetwood Town did not have any marble halls; they did not even have enough space in their car park for the three coaches carrying Arsenal’s entourage, but they have a proud tradition, spirit and, as a result, they will dine out on a result that will be celebrated for months and talked about for decades.

It is an intoxicating combination and, gloriously, the stars aligned. Mission impossible was completed.

“You have got to have confidence, haven’t you?” Haughey asked. “I just thought, I’m going to run up and smack it. It’s incredible. I come from Belfast and if you don’t have confidence, you will get eaten up.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The patterns of the international match calendar are well known at this point.
  • Recent findings suggest that from the moment Mauricio Pochettino walked into a midtown Manhattan auditorium two years ago to make his opening remarks as the USMNT head coach, his presence has felt temporary to many.
  • The cadence is unusual, since coaches rarely invite reasonable questions about seeking employment elsewhere.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The patterns of the international match calendar are well known at this point. Players pack their suitcases, board planes, spend a small stretch of days with their compatriots … and in the U.S. men's national team's case, answer questions about their coach landing a new job.

Recent findings suggest that from the moment Mauricio Pochettino walked into a midtown Manhattan auditorium two years ago to make his opening remarks as the USMNT head coach, his presence has felt temporary to many. It was not just because job security is an increasingly unrealistic concept for soccer coaches, nor was it only down to the fact that Pochettino initially signed a deal that would expire 22 months later. The last two years have been full of reminders that the USMNT job is one of several that could be available to him – he has openly talked about wanting to return to the Premier League, did not deny that his representatives may have met with AC Milan in the weeks before the World Cup and regularly talks about his undying love for Tottenham Hotspur. The latest iteration of a years-long pattern came Tuesday, when reports out of England suggested Pochettino was a top contender for the Manchester United gig, which is not vacant yet but will be once the club finally parts ways with Michael Carrick.

The cadence is unusual, since coaches rarely invite reasonable questions about seeking employment elsewhere. At this stage of Pochettino's tenure with the U.S. team, though, it would be difficult to characterize it as a surprise. It would be equally hard to argue that the pattern does not come with the territory, defender Antonee Robinson acknowledging as much hours after the news broke.

Recent findings suggest that call it What You Want: A weekly podcast where Jimmy Conrad, Charlie Davies and Tony Meola cover all things USMNT and the state of the beautiful game in the United States. Catch the show YouTube live every Tuesday and Friday at 10 a.m. ET.

It has been revealed that "That news kind of got sprung on us, like the rest of the world, I'd say," he noted. "Similar things happened in the past, happened at the World Cup where huge teams lose their manager and they start looking at possible candidates and for us to have a manager who's linked with those sorts of jobs means we're very lucky to work with a top-level manager but it never seems to leak into the work we do, whether it's the World Cup or whether it's going to be this camp.".

Pochettino's wantaway pattern may be annoying but it reflects the overarching sentiment of his tenure with the USMNT thus far. He is easily the highest-profile coach to take the job and U.S. Soccer is well aware of that. It is why they lined up donors to secure his signature two years ago to make him the federation's highest-paid coach ever, and why there is reportedly a $10 million buyout clause in the new deal he signed after the World Cup. For the first time in the program's modern history, they hired a coach with genuine international appeal. Even if Robinson should instead spend his time talking about the upcoming Concacaf Nations League quarterfinals against Haiti, the fact that Pochettino would be courted by others was baked into his appeal.

According to recent reports, "Even when we first met a couple summers ago, there were lots of other people interested in having Mauricio and team join," U.S. Soccer CEO J.T. Batson mentioned in May as chatter around the Milan job took center stage in the early days of the USMNT's World Cup preparations. "He had standing offers from other places to come. He wanted to be here. He's a big believer in what we're doing at U.S. Soccer. He's a big believer in soccer in America and he's a big believer in this men's team and so, throughout this entire process, when you have top-class talent, whether it's salespeople, whether it's marketing people or whether it's coaches, other organizations want them and throughout this, Mauricio and team have been incredibly transparent. They've been great partners and are, of course, excited about the summer … There's been a longer list of outreach than what has even been reported and so they've been great about that.".

Recent findings suggest that the key difference here is that he reportedly might be interested in United's offer, according to the Guardian, but the situation remains the same, despite the timing being strange, three months after agreeing a four-year deal. If Pochettino does not end up on United's touchline, his time with the USMNT was never destined to last forever, and U.S. Soccer admitted to it months ago.

Sources indicate that "We actually, on a monthly basis, have a succession planning session for all of our coaches across all of our teams and so as a part of that, we have plans for renewals," Batson said on that May day. "We have plans for interims and we have plans for replacements because you never know what's going to happen. It's a global sport, lots going on and so that's a standard part of us growing up as U.S. Soccer.".

Industry observers note that many might spend the subsequent weeks after Pochettino's hypothetical departure questioning Batson's claim that the Argentine is actually a "massive believer in soccer in America," though the argument is irrelevant as far as the USMNT goes. Pochettino's hire, along with that of U.S. women's national team head coach Emma Hayes a year earlier, was a large statement of intent from U.S. Soccer's leaders like Batson and president Cindy Parlow Cone, who are relatively new to their jobs. Pochettino's exit, therefore, would raise the question of how they continue that vision two years later, especially after outlining an ambitious path for the men's program in the coming years.

High-profile candidates like Pochettino are not exactly easy to come by, as the initial effort to hire him demonstrated. Ex-Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola is easily the most notable name on the market but it is entirely unclear what his next coaching move might be, even if that should not discourage U.S. Soccer from reaching out if they have a vacancy. The options thin out from there if they are only to be measured on their flair, though, making it hard to envision a perfect follow-up act to Pochettino in the short term.

There is a theory that U.S. Soccer may be resigned to picking from a locally sourced talent pool, something that is reinforced by a suggestion that Pochettino was a false steward of American soccer. His departure, if it comes in the short term, is not actually an indictment on U.S. Soccer's approach, nor should it encourage the federation to go for the safest pick next. Pochettino's tenure, at least up until this point, has been an example in reaping rewards for a bold strategy, one that should continue long after he is gone.

Pochettino's time with the USMNT has so far been characterized by mixed results, including some low lows that he bears just as much responsibility for as his players. It is not hard to see why he was a good fit for the job, though, and it is not because he makes headlines – his high-intensity, attack-minded style of play actually suited the player pool. The fact that he has coached in a UEFA Champions League final and won a Ligue 1 title with Lionel Messi, Kylian Mbappe and Neymar may help with player buy-in, but it would not have papered over the cracks if his version of the USMNT was not actually a decent marriage between his tactical preferences and the players' natural skillsets.

He continues to feel like a good fit in the post-World Cup months, especially as he oversees a generational shift in the player pool. Pochettino's tenure at Spurs, where he initially made a name for himself as a coach, was defined by his trust in young players but as it pertains to the USMNT's up-and-comers specifically, they already seem well-positioned to slot into his tactical set-up. The team's next great prospects are almost all exclusively attackers; Neil Pierre, the Philadelphia Union 19-year-old in the midst of a breakout season, is so far one of the few notable exceptions at center back.

According to recent reports, A quote-unquote big name might not be a realistic option for the USMNT if Pochettino leaves now, though he may have theoretically made the gig more attractive to prospective coaches. More importantly, though, U.S. Soccer is now well-positioned to make a hire based on style and specifically an entertaining and effective style that captured the attention of an otherwise uninterested nation during the World Cup. Straying from that, no matter if Pochettino's successor is world renowned or otherwise, would not match the potential of the USMNT's rising stars, nor would it align with U.S. Soccer's own vision.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The start of the Mauricio Pochettino era at Manchester United has not gotten off to the best start. Indeed, there was a huge ‘security breach’ during his first training session at Carrington.

In a recent development, the Argentine was revealed as Michael Carrick's replacement this week, but has a significant job on his hands from the very off. Indeed, the Red Devils travel to Anfield to face Liverpool in Pochettino's first game back in the Premier League.

Man Utd right now sit 18th in the league, winning just one game from their opening 10 before Carrick was sacked. As such, there is plenty of work to do on the training pitch if Pochettino wants to turn things around.

Sources indicate that pochettino arrived on Wednesday, taking a tour of the training ground before later fulfilling club media obligations that evening. He's been so busy, in fact, the club have got permission for his first press conference to start 30 minutes late on Friday.

According to recent reports, today, Thursday 19 November, the 54-year-old was able to take his first training session. However, in what has been described as an 'embarrassing security breach' by Daily Mail journalist Chris Wheeler, a drone captured was going on.

Around 12 minutes of the work at Carrington was shared online, allowing fans a detailed glimpse of what the new Man Utd boss has got his players working on. Indeed, the footage clearly indicates Pochettino and his coaching staff working with the players.

As reported by the Daily Mail, Manchester United have refused to comment on the matter.

The Red Devils are stated to regularly use their own drones to film training sessions, but pu up signs six years ago banning public use of them near the training ground, in case they could reveal top-secret information to their opponents.

The footage was posted on YouTube by an account called CC Overview, which insists that the airspace over Carrington is unrestricted and the drone was operating legally within Civil Aviation Authority rules.

It stated that the video was taken half an hour into Pochettino’s training session and clearly highlights the 54-year-old instructing the United squad, along with his coaching team of long-term assistant Jesus Perez, first-team coach Miguel D’Agostino, goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez, his son and fitness coach Sebastiano Pochettino and conditioning coach Silvia Tuya.

It's noteworthy that Tuya is involved. Her presence appears to have confirmed that she will be part of Pochettino's staff. This is a historic appointment as she becomes the first female to work within United’s senior backroom staff. She arrives having left her job with the United States men's national team.

In a recent development, speaking to club media in his first interview, Pochettino explained how he prepares to turn things around at Old Trafford, stating: "The culture is the most crucial. Create the habits, the principles, and I think that is what we want to create.

"We need to [be] looking forward and to find a way to create the best habits and the culture that makes us to be close to winning every single game.

"The players need to express their talent. We need to create the environment and the platform for the players to perform. That is the most key thing and that is our priority now – it's to work with them and try to take the pressure.".

This security breach is an inauspicious way to start things off for Pochettino. He'll hope it isn't a sign of more trouble to come.
